---
title: "Start bridge: generic pages and the conversion codemod"
description: "Render App Router pages generically in Start's RSC environment and convert a Next satellite onto @tuturuuu/start-bridge with one command."
---

This page extends the [Start bridge](/build/devops/start-bridge) v0 contract
with two additive pieces: an RSC-based **generic page adapter**, so a converted
app needs no hand-written page models, and a **codemod** that converts a Next
satellite with no hand edits. Production is unchanged; conversion produces a
staging candidate only.

## Generic page adapter (RSC mode)

Next pages are async server components with `'use client'` islands. Start's RSC
environment (`@tanstack/react-start` RSC mode with `@vitejs/plugin-rsc`) runs
that code with the same boundaries Next enforces, so retained page source
renders unchanged.

Per request, a Start server function in the app (generated
`src/start-bridge/page-route.tsx`) calls `resolveBridgePage` from
`start/page-render`:

1. Resolve the location the app sees (`start/page-location`): on SSR the
   request the handler forwarded after `proxy.ts`, so rewrites apply while the
   browser keeps its URL; on client navigation the app proxy runs for the
   target, so the same URL renders the same page, a proxy redirect becomes a
   Start redirect and any other terminal response reloads the document.
   Match that app-relative path (mount stripped; a leading locale segment
   addresses a manifest with a stripped `[locale]`) against the generated
   page manifest. A localized page for the stripped path wins over a dynamic
   segment that would capture the locale (`/en` is the landing page, not
   workspace `en`); a page whose first segment is literally the locale still
   wins. No match answers 404.
2. Load the page and its layout/template chain from the generated
   `page-modules.bridge.gen.ts` (lazy imports keyed by the manifest `file`).
3. Pass Next's props: `params` and `searchParams` as Promises; repeated query
   keys become arrays. A stripped `[locale]` segment resolves from the
   middleware `x-next-intl-locale` header, then `NEXT_LOCALE`, then the default.
4. Merge `metadata`/`generateMetadata` and `viewport` like Next (shallow merge,
   nearest `title.template`) and convert them to `head()` data.
5. Lift the root layout's `<html>`/`<body>` attributes into the Start shell
   (`createBridgeRootRoute`). Server-component wrappers and the RSC CSS
   fragment around the root layout are expanded first; client references are
   never called.
6. Await async pages and layouts before streaming, so `notFound()` and
   `redirect()` in their bodies answer 404 and redirect. Sync server
   components stay elements because they may call hooks.
7. Return the tree through `renderServerComponent`; the catch-all and index
   routes render it, on SSR and on client navigation alike.

| Piece | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `startBridgePreset({ rsc: true })` | Enables Start RSC mode on top of the bridge's `next-intl/*` and `next/root-params` shims; the adapter feeds the resolved `[locale]` to `next/root-params` |
| `startBridgeRscPlugin()` (`vite/rsc`) | Resolves `next/navigation`, `next-intl` and `next-intl/navigation` per environment (server variants in `rsc`), makes `next/font/*` inert, names the rsc entries `<name>.js` because plugin-rsc imports that name from SSR while Void emits `.mjs`, and adds `rscEntries` |
| `start/server-actions` | React `'use server'` calls go through a Start server function (TanStack disables plugin-rsc's action handler); arguments use React's reply encoding, so form actions receive their `FormData` (sent as JSON entries with base64 files, because the function proxy accepts JSON POSTs only; uploads over 10 MB belong in storage); Start's CSRF middleware applies |
| `request-context` | The store is keyed on a global symbol: the rsc and SSR environments bundle separate module copies in one isolate |

### Route handlers run in the rsc environment

plugin-rsc rejects `server-only` in every environment except `rsc`, and the
Worker entry is bundled in `ssr`. The generated `vite.config.mts` registers the
API registry as the `bridge-api` rsc entry (`rscEntries`), and
`cloudflare/worker.ts` loads it with
`import.meta.viteRsc.loadModule('rsc', 'bridge-api')` before building the
handler. Route modules (and the `server-only` packages they import) are
compiled once, in `rsc`; the request store is global, so `next/headers`,
cookies and the mount see the same request. Never alias or disable plugin-rsc's
import validation to make a build pass.

`redirect()` from `next/navigation` keeps an absolute URL absolute, as in
Next. Start's router reduces a same-origin absolute href to its path, and on
the apex Web's `https://tuturuuu.com/login` is same-origin with
`tuturuuu.com/<app>`, so the bridge marks the target for its response
finalization (which otherwise adds the mount) and sets `reloadDocument` for
client navigation. Without it, a mounted app's login redirect loops into its
own `/<app>/login`.

Fonts from `next/font` resolve to inert objects; load font CSS through the app
stylesheet. A page that needs Next behaviour the adapter lacks (parallel or
intercepting routes) stays a hand-written page via `owned`/`ignored` in
`start-bridge.routes.json`.

## Converting an app

```bash
node scripts/start-bridge-codemod/cli.mjs <app>            # dry run: unified diff + coverage
node scripts/start-bridge-codemod/cli.mjs <app> --apply    # write files, run bun add
node scripts/start-bridge-codemod/cli.mjs <app> --report   # coverage only
node scripts/start-bridge-codemod/cli.mjs <app> --apply --hold  # cutover prep: add the held record
```

The dry run reads only. `--apply` writes the same change set and installs the
pinned toolchain through `bun add --exact` in the app workspace; dependencies
are never edited into `package.json` by hand. The toolchain includes the
repository's exact `@cloudflare/workers-types` pin, which the native binding
type check resolves from the app. The app's `.gitignore` gains `.void/` and
`.void-wrangler.jsonc` (local `vp build` output) when missing, appended after
its own lines. Re-running an applied app, including one
that already added a pin by hand, is a no-op. Every owned file carries a "Generated by the start-bridge codemod"
marker; an unmarked hand-written file is a conflict that blocks `--apply`
unless `--adopt` is passed. Codegen errors (an unregistered `route.*`/`page.*`),
a missing `src/proxy.ts` and, with `--hold`, a missing Vercel publisher also
block. Owned
files and the app's JSON edits are formatted with the repository's Biome.

The codemod writes or edits:

- `start-bridge.routes.json` (hand-maintained `owned`/`ignored` entries win on
  re-runs) and the bridge codegen registries, plus `page-modules.bridge.gen.ts`
  and `public-assets.bridge.gen.ts`.
- `vite.config.mts` (preset in RSC mode), `void.config.ts` (the held
  `tuturuuu-<app>-vite-staging` Worker with `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1` and the
  `nodejs_compat` and `global_fetch_strictly_public` flags; the latter sends
  same-zone self-fetches such as app-base `appUrl(path, request.url)` to the
  Worker instead of the zone origin, the retained Vercel app),
  `cloudflare/worker.ts` (`mounts`: `<app>.tuturuuu.com` root and the
  `tuturuuu.com/<app>` mount), `tsconfig.cloudflare.json`.
- `src/start.ts` (`bridgeServerFnFetch`), `src/router.tsx`
  (`routerBasepath()`, `ssr: { nonce: requestNonce() }`), the
  root/index/catch-all routes and `routeTree.gen.ts`. The Worker does not
  enforce `csp` by default: each app adds `createBridgeHandler({ csp })` with
  a policy that fits its scripts before it mounts on the apex.
- Package scripts `build:cloudflare`, `dev:cloudflare`, `preview:cloudflare`
  (`--configLoader runner`), `routes:check` and `type-check:cloudflare`. `build` stays `next build`, so
  the current Vercel deployment is unchanged.
- `.env.example` moves to `env.example`: Void accepts only `.env`.
- The `biome.json` override that keeps every generated `routeTree.gen.ts`
  out of Biome (formatter, linter and assist off), once for the repository.
  TanStack's generator rewrites the file in its own format on each build, and
  `bun check:changed` passes changed files to Biome explicitly.
- With `--hold` only, the held record: `tuturuuu.ci.ts`
  `productionPublicationPolicy`, the protected surface in
  `scripts/ci/production-publication-policy.ts` and its regression's app list,
  and the `production-policy` gate in `vercel-production-<app>.yaml` (as for
  Shortener).
- `tsconfig.json` excludes the Start-only sources, so the existing Next
  `type-check` is unchanged; `type-check:cloudflare` checks them against
  `tsconfig.cloudflare.json`.

<Warning>
A held record also holds that app's `vercel-production-<app>.yaml`, so the
current Vercel production deployment freezes until the cutover admits the app.
Conversion PRs therefore run without `--hold`; the app's cutover-prep PR adds
the hold and merges just before the flip.
</Warning>

### Worker options

`start-bridge.config.ts` at the app root is app-owned: the codemod creates
it once (with the shared response policy below) and never updates or replaces it. The
generated `cloudflare/worker.ts` passes its options on, so an app changes
Worker behaviour without editing generated files:

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `csp(nonce, { request, response, path })` | `createBridgeHandler({ csp })`: the response's Content-Security-Policy; the generated router already stamps the nonce. Return `null` to keep the response's own policy. Framable paths (`@tuturuuu/utils/framable-paths`, e.g. Web's uploaded WebGL builds with their `sandbox` CSP) always keep the upstream policy untouched |
| `framablePaths` | App-relative path regexes other origins may frame, beyond the platform list in `@tuturuuu/utils/framable-paths`. The generated Worker passes them to the handler `csp` and the response policy, which leave their upstream CSP untouched and set no `X-Frame-Options` |
| `mounts` | Overrides the generated hosts, `basePath` or `unknownHost` (`'reject'` answers 404 for unlisted hosts) |
| `apiOrigin(request, { env, path })` | Origin for one unowned `/api/*` request (e.g. Storefront's `/api/v1/inventory/**` to Inventory); `undefined` keeps the central Web API. Forwarding keeps the central forward's base stripping, loop guard and header removal |
| `wrapResponse(response, { request, env, mounts, publicAssets })` | Decorates every response; use the shared response policy below. The Worker passes its effective mounts and public files |
| `worker: { workersDev?, compatibilityFlags? }` | Generated Worker settings, applied when the codemod runs: `workers_dev` (default off when `mounts.unknownHost` is `'reject'`, otherwise on) and flags added to the always-on `nodejs_compat` and `global_fetch_strictly_public` (e.g. AI's `enable_request_signal`). They reach `void.config.ts`, the sealed artifact identity and the runtime test, which fails if the config changed without a re-run. A `workers.dev` root host with `workers_dev` off is a codemod problem |

API paths the app owns but forwards (Storefront's Inventory APIs) are listed
client-safely in `start-bridge.routes.json` as
`"api": { "forwarded": ["/api/v1/inventory/[...path]"] }`. The codegen merges
them into `appApiPatterns`, so the shared app-base resolver mounts them like
local routes, and the Worker, finding no local handler, forwards them through
`apiOrigin`. `start-bridge.config.ts` holds server code and is never imported
by the browser. The codemod and the runtime test load it with Node's type
stripping, so keep its imports strippable (packages, or relative paths with
their `.ts` extension).

### Response policy

Every app uses one tested policy instead of hand-rolled `wrapResponse` code,
which in four separate reviews kept repeating the same three bugs:
- caching set only as a default, so a handler's `public, max-age` survived;
- an asset exemption that ignored the method, so `POST /assets/x` escaped;
- an existing CSP passed through without `frame-ancestors`.

```ts
import {
  appRobots,
  createRootResponsePolicy,
} from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/response-policy';
import { defineBridgeAppConfig } from '@tuturuuu/start-bridge/start/app-config';

export default defineBridgeAppConfig({
  wrapResponse: createRootResponsePolicy({ seo: appRobots }),
  framablePaths: [/^\/embed\//u], // only if other origins may frame these paths
});
```

- **Every response** gets:
  - `X-Robots-Tag` from `seo`. `appRobots` reads the app's `seo-policy.json` entry, which the codemod emits into the generated Worker (no runtime JSON). A response is left indexable only on the public allowlist on the canonical origin, outside reserved paths (`api`, `login`, `dashboard`, `embed`, ..., in any letter case, as Next's header sources match). Each path segment is decoded once before both checks, so `/%61uth` is `/auth`, and a malformed escape, an encoded `/` or `\`, or a double encoding stays private. Staging deployments (`TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`) are never indexable either. Everything else gets `PRIVATE_ROBOTS_HEADER`. An upstream `noindex` is never overridden;
  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`;
  - outside framable paths, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, and `frame-ancestors 'none'` in every CSP policy. An existing `frame-ancestors` is replaced in any letter case, each comma-separated or repeated header policy is covered, and a response without a CSP gets `csp` (default `frame-ancestors 'none'`).
- **Caching:** only `GET`/`HEAD` requests for `/assets/*` or the app's public files keep their own caching, unless they answer HTML. Every other response is set, not defaulted, to `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and gains `Vary: Cookie`.
- **Framable paths:** the platform list (`@tuturuuu/utils/framable-paths`, Web's uploaded WebGL builds at `/api/v1/workspaces/*/external-projects/assets/*/webgl`), the app's `framablePaths` and the policy's own `framable`. These keep the upstream CSP byte-for-byte, or its absence, and any upstream `X-Frame-Options` (`DENY`/`SAMEORIGIN`) is removed. Web's `sandbox allow-scripts ...` policy must reach the browser, or uploaded scripts run unsandboxed on the app origin. The handler `csp` skips these paths too. Matching is case-sensitive, unlike Next's header `source` matching; that's harmless because central's routes are case-sensitive. One stateless matcher is shared by the handler and the policy: `g`/`y` patterns are cloned without those flags, so `lastIndex` never changes a result.
- **Failures:** a throw in the proxy, an endpoint, Start or the route load answers the bridge's generic `500 Internal Server Error`. The details go only to `console.error`, and the response still goes through `wrapResponse`, so it gets no-store, robots and framing headers too. Hand-rolled wrappers that apps keep until they migrate also receive this generic 500, where a handler throw used to escape uncaught. They still run, and still see no error details.
- **Paths:** framable and asset paths are matched app-relative, so on the `tuturuuu.com/<app>` mount the base is stripped first. WebSocket upgrades (101) pass through untouched.

Migrating an app with a hand-rolled `wrapResponse` (Finance, Tasks, Track,
Storefront):

1. Replace the function with `createRootResponsePolicy({ seo, framable? })`.
   Keep the app's robots value as `seo`, for example `'noindex, nofollow, nosnippet'`.
2. Drop any import of `./src/start-bridge/public-assets.bridge.gen`. The Worker
   now passes `publicAssets`, and an extensionless relative import cannot be
   loaded by the codemod or the runtime test, which read the config with Node's
   type stripping.
3. Keep `csp` (the nonce policy) as it is. The response policy adds
   `frame-ancestors 'none'` to it.
4. Re-run the codemod for the app, so its `cloudflare/worker.ts` passes
   `mounts` and `publicAssets`, then run `bun check:changed`.

### Route handlers load lazily

The generated API registry (`api.lazy`) imports each route on its first
request (`lazyRouteModule`), with the route's HTTP methods read statically
from its source so `OPTIONS` and `405` need no import. One route's
dependencies (for example a Node-only SDK chain) therefore cannot fail the
Worker at startup; a route that re-exports with `export *` stays eager. In
the rsc build, CommonJS `require()` of Node built-ins becomes an ESM import
served by `nodejs_compat`, and `.wasm`/`.bin` imports become Wrangler
CompiledWasm/Data modules (as `next/og`'s Workers port needs). An app whose
Worker code runs in native SSR (`rsc: { enabled: false }`, as Calendar does)
opts its `ssr` environment into the same conversion by adding
`startBridgeNodeBuiltinsPlugin()` from `@tuturuuu/start-bridge/vite/rsc` to its
Vite plugins; rsc apps need nothing. A route that
needs a Node API workerd does not provide still fails when it is hit; serve it
from Web (`centralFirst`) or port it.

### Native CI

When the repository has the reusable `.github/workflows/native-start-app.yaml`
(#6753), the codemod also writes the app's qualification CI, modelled on
Shortener:

- `.github/workflows/<app>-cloudflare.yaml`: a thin `workflow_call` caller with
  path filters for the app, its transitive workspace dependencies, the template
  and the shared native CI scripts, and Shortener's inputs. An app without a
  `test` script runs its Vitest suite with `--passWithNoTests`. Registered in
  `tuturuuu.ci.ts`.
- `scripts/ci/<app>-native-artifact.py`: the app's Worker identity and public
  files over `scripts/ci/apps-native-artifact.py`.
- `cloudflare/native-built-worker.runtime.mjs` (`test:runtime`, run with
  `node --test` after the build; not a `*.test.*` file, so source test runs
  never pick it up): a generic
  emitted-Worker smoke run on the sealed artifact, with all egress denied:
  Worker identity, public-file parity, build identity when the app has
  `/api/build-info` (read anonymously, as production smoke does: an app whose
  proxy guards API routes must admit exact `GET`/`HEAD /api/build-info`), the page outcomes the app declares, no server error on an unknown path, and
  the response policy (no-store, `X-Robots-Tag`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and
  `frame-ancestors 'none'`) on real responses, after checking their status and
  content: a page rendering 200 HTML (by default the first `runtime` path
  expecting 200), a 200 JSON API response (`/api/build-info`) and a 404 HTML
  page (`/__native-smoke-missing__`). `runtimeProbes` in
  `start-bridge.routes.json` overrides a probe's path, or skips it with
  `{ "skip": "<reason>" }`. A skipped page or 404 probe must also name the
  app's own runtime test that covers it, as
  `"fixture": "cloudflare/<name>.runtime.mjs"`. For example, an auth-only app
  whose `/` redirects to login names its isolated-auth fixture. The fixture must
  be a distinct app-owned file that `test:runtime`'s `cloudflare/*.runtime.mjs`
  glob selects: never the generated gate itself, and never a dotfile, which the
  glob skips. The codemod and the gate both check this and that the fixture
  exists, and at least one probe must always run. A probe the codemod can neither default nor find declared, or a
  set that skips every probe, is a codemod problem.
  The test reads the Worker's effective mounts (the generated defaults plus
  `mounts` in the app-owned `start-bridge.config.ts`, loaded with Node's type
  stripping, so keep that file's imports strippable) and probes with raw
  `Host` headers: every configured root host serves `/`. A mounted app serves
  every declared page on `tuturuuu.com/<app>`. A root-only app (no
  `tuturuuu.com` in `mountHosts`) must set `unknownHost: 'reject'`, and the
  bridge must reject its apex paths and an unknown host with its own 404
  before any app code runs, with no egress. Page
  outcomes come from `runtime` in `start-bridge.routes.json` (default
  `{ "/": 200 }`): a record that must declare `/`, mapping app-relative paths
  to an exact status or `{ "redirect": "<path or absolute URL>" }`. A path
  redirect must stay on the requested origin and, on the apex, keep the
  `/<app>` mount, so a login redirect, a cross-origin hop or a jump to
  another app never passes. The codemod rejects empty, array or root-less
  maps, and `scripts/start-bridge-codemod/runtime-outcome.mjs` holds the
  shared checks. App-specific acceptance goes in further
  `cloudflare/*.runtime.mjs` files, which `test:runtime`
  (`node --test cloudflare/*.runtime.mjs`) runs with it.

There is no publisher: production stays with the held record and the
cutover PR.

### Signed-in root browser gate

`scripts/ci/native-root-browser.mjs` checks what the generated runtime test
cannot reach: signed-in SSR and client hydration in a real browser. It runs on
a build host with Chromium (Thanh) against the app's restored, sealed artifact:

```bash
python3 scripts/ci/<app>-native-artifact.py restore apps/<app> --archive native.tar.gz --receipt restored.json
<APP>_SOURCE_SHA=<sha> node scripts/ci/native-root-browser.mjs <app> --receipt restored.json
```

The gate:

- Verifies the artifact against the receipt, starts it in local workerd at
  the app's root host, and checks that build-info names the exact source.
- Signs a disposable app session with a random coordination secret.
- Answers every Supabase and Web request in-process: the fixture user, the
  profile's rows and Web responses, empty reads, and 401 for any other Web
  API read. Any other Worker or browser request fails the run.
- For each locale, follows the signed-in SSR redirects. They must stay on the
  root host and end on a `200` page with `<html lang>`, emitted assets and
  `private, no-store`. Chromium then loads the same path and must hydrate.
- Fails on page errors or failed `/assets/*`, and re-verifies the artifact
  at the end.

The gate only drives a Worker it started on loopback. It takes no URL and
refuses a non-loopback origin, so it never runs against a hosted deployment.
Hosted signed-in acceptance stays a staging step with real accounts.

Each app owns its profile at `apps/<app>/cloudflare/root-browser.profile.mjs`
(a default-export object, no imports):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `rootHost` | Canonical `<app>.tuturuuu.com` host the Worker serves |
| `robots` | Expected `X-Robots-Tag` on SSR responses (optional) |
| `session` | Fixture cookies: `app` (`tuturuuu_app_session` for the app), `web` (`tuturuuu_web_app_session`) |
| `locales` | `{ locale, path, finalPath, cookies? }`: start path, the `RegExp` the signed-in chain must end on, extra cookies (e.g. `NEXT_LOCALE`) |
| `supabase` | Table name to a row factory `({ actorId, wsId }) => row`, returned for `GET /rest/v1/<table>` |
| `web` | `'GET /api/...'` to a response factory for Web API reads the page needs |
| `hydration` | `request(context)`: a path prefix the client must request, or `text(context)`: a marker only the client renders. Polling pages never reach network idle |
| `browser` | Extra browser origins: `{ origin, fulfill: 'image' \| 401 }` (e.g. a default avatar host) |

Regressions for the profile, session, egress and SSR rules run with
`node --test scripts/ci/native-root-browser.test.mjs`.

### Generator inputs

The codemod reads app-specific behaviour from the app's existing
configuration, so apps regenerate instead of forking generated files:

| Input | Read from | Generated result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Proxy matcher | `src/proxy.ts` `export const config = { matcher }` | `matches: createProxyMatcher(proxyConfig.matcher, defaultProxyMatches)` in `cloudflare/worker.ts`; Next's path-to-regexp evaluates each source on the app-relative path (`has`/`missing` entries always run the proxy) |
| `centralFirst` | `next.config.*` calling `createTuturuuuWebWorkspaceApiRewrites` (`beforeFiles`) | `src/start-bridge/central-first.ts` re-exports `TUTURUUU_WEB_WORKSPACE_API_RESERVED_PATHS`; the Worker and the app-base resolver share it |
| `next/og` | any `next/og` import under `src/` | preset `og: '@cloudflare/pages-plugin-vercel-og/api'` (as Meet) and the pinned dependency |
| Assets binding | `@tuturuuu/start-bridge` exports `./assets` (#6753) | the Worker env types `ASSETS: AssetsBinding` (`import type` from `@tuturuuu/start-bridge/assets`), which the Workers `Fetcher` satisfies; the handler serves it through `fetchAsset` |
| Internal API app base | `@tuturuuu/internal-api` exports `registerDefaultAppBaseResolver` (#6764) and the app depends on it | `src/start-bridge/app-base.ts` registers `createAppBaseResolver(appApiPatterns, centralFirst)` from the codegen's client-safe `api-patterns.bridge.gen.ts`: app-owned routes are mounted in the browser and absolute on the request host on the server; Web routes are untouched |

The preset renders `@tuturuuu/vercel`'s Analytics and Speed Insights as
nothing, because Workers serve no `/_vercel/*` scripts; an app with an explicit
`shims` list opts in with `inertVercel: true`.

Each environment bundle (browser, SSR, rsc) carries its own internal-api
module, so the registration is imported by `src/router.tsx`, the page route
and the rsc API entry (`src/start-bridge/api-entry.ts`).

### Coverage report

The report classifies each page through its layouts and local import graph. A
page is generic unless it reaches an unshimmed framework specifier or a
parallel/intercepting segment. The shim list follows the bridge preset;
`'use server'` modules and `next/og` are features, not blockers.

### Verification

Codemod regressions run with `node scripts/start-bridge-codemod/<file>.test.mjs`
on disposable fixture repositories; edits to repository files are tested
against the real anchors. Each converted app still needs exact-commit CI:
unit, types, lint, the real `vp build`, the sealed artifact and the
emitted-runtime and browser acceptance.
